To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“FOLFOX related IP is associated with high morbidity and mortality, that the prognosis of the patient with respiratory insufficiency is grim, that every patient who survives intubation and ventilation recovers fully and that additional immune-modulating treatment is warranted.

FOLFOX-induced IP is a life-threatening complication of chemotherapy, that discontinuation of oxaliplatin is insufficient to prevent mortality and that the introduction of immune modulators in the treatment regimen is essential to prevent mortality and promote full recovery.

the prognosis of FOLFOX-treated patients with respiratory symptoms is poor (death rate 76.9%), that the prognosis of the intubated patient is even worse (death rate 100%), but that the patient who survived intubatation and mechanical ventilation always recovers completely.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a new treatment option for the patient with FOLFOX-induced interstitial pneumonia.
the need to improve the prognosis of the critically ill cancer patient who develops FOLFOX-related respiratory insufficiency.

the identification and treatment of FOLFIRI-induced lung toxicity and with the development of a therapeutic algorithm that may be of help to clinicians confronted with the problem of FOLFIRi-related lung toxicity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FOLFOX-related IP is a potentially fatal complication, but one that is treatable with multimodal immune modulatory therapy.
the discontinuation of oxaliplatin in the patient with respiratory symptoms is not sufficient and that the use of immune globulins, cyclophosphamid and other agents may be life saving.
FOLFOX-related pulmonary side effects are rare, but potentially lethal and that early intervention with a broad range of immune modulating agents may be lifesaving.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the FOLFOX regimen is an effective and well-tolerated drug cocktail for the treatment of colorectal and gastric cancers but that the risk of developing interstitial pneumonia is not negligible, especially when the patient is older than 70 years.
the prognosis for the FOLFOX-related respiratory insufficient patient is poor but that a multimodal treatment approach may result in a full recovery of lung function in the surviving patients.
the prognosis of FOLFOX related interstitial pneumonia is poor and that early and aggressive treatment with immune modulating agents may improve the prognosis of the critically ill patient.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the prognosis of FOLFOX-associated IP is poor, and that a more comprehensive treatment strategy should be considered in order to improve the prognosis of these patients.
the use of FOLFOX in the elderly should be considered carefully and that the use of immune-modulating agents should be considered in the event of respiratory insufficiency.
a multimodal immune-modulating approach may be beneficial in patients who develop severe respiratory insufficiency in the course of chemotherapy with the FOLFOX regimen.
